title: Why raise me blind, when I could see before?
subtitle: Sight that was never used
then: The one who turned from Allah's reminder will ask {trap}why have You raised me blind, when I had sight?{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains he means sight in the life of this world. Mujahid said being blind means {trap}having no proof{/trap} to offer.
now: You see everything on your phone: news, sports, every friend's holiday. Hours of looking each day. {idea}Seeing a lot is not the same as seeing what matters.{/idea} Use your eyes today for one sign of Allah.
old: I see plenty. I know what is going on in the world.
new: Real sight is noticing Allah's signs. Without that, I am looking but blind.
try: Spend five minutes today looking at something in nature and naming it as His sign.

title: You forgot Our signs, so today you are forgotten.
subtitle: The reply matches the deed
then: Ibn Kathir explains: the signs came and {trap}you dealt with them like one who does not remember them{/trap}, neglecting and ignoring them. So today you are treated like one forgotten. He notes this threat is {idea}not about forgetting memorised words while still acting on the Quran{/idea}.
now: You are trying to memorise a surah and keep losing the middle verses. That is not what this verse is about. {idea}It is about living as if the message never arrived.{/idea} Keeping its meaning alive in your day is the remedy.
old: If I forget the words I learned, I am in this verse.
new: The warning is for turning away from the signs. Living by them keeps me remembered.
try: Pick one verse you know and act on its meaning once today.

title: The Hereafter's loss is heavier and lasts longer.
subtitle: Weighing now against later
then: Allah says this is how He repays {trap}the one who transgresses and does not believe in His signs{/trap}. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter{/idea}. The warning is meant to steer choices now.
now: You hide a mistake at work to avoid embarrassment, knowing it hurts someone. Owning up costs you a bad afternoon. {idea}A hard moment here is lighter than carrying it there.{/idea}
old: Avoiding embarrassment now is worth almost anything.
new: A loss in this world is small next to what lasts. I can choose the lighter cost.
try: Own up today to one small thing you have been hiding to save face.

title: You walk through the homes of nations now gone.
subtitle: Empty houses that teach
then: Ibn Kathir explains the people of Makkah {trap}walked among the empty homes{/trap} of nations who denied their messengers. In that are signs {idea}for those with sound intellect{/idea}. He cites: it is not the eyes that grow blind, but the hearts.
now: You stroll through an old castle on holiday, take a selfie in a ruined palace. Someone once thought it would last forever. {idea}The ruins are a message, not just a backdrop.{/idea}
old: Old ruins are interesting history, nothing more.
new: Every empty palace says: what I build without Allah will not last.
try: Next time you pass an old or abandoned building, think about who once lived there.

title: Only His word and a set time hold it back.
subtitle: The delay is mercy, not absence
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah had already given His word that {reward}He would not punish anyone until the proof was established{/reward}, and at a time He set. Otherwise, {trap}the punishment would seize them immediately{/trap}.
now: You did something wrong last month and nothing happened. Life went on. It is tempting to think it did not matter. {idea}The quiet is a window to come back{/idea}, not proof that it is fine.
old: If nothing bad happened, I got away with it.
new: Allah's delay is time given to me to turn back, not a sign it does not count.
try: Use today's quiet to fix one wrong that no one has called you out on.

title: Be patient with their words, and praise through the day.
subtitle: Prayer as the answer to mockery
then: Allah comforted the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}be patient with what they say{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says before sunrise refers to Fajr and before sunset to Asr. The Prophet ﷺ, looking at a full moon, said {reward}you will see your Lord as you see this moon{/reward}, so do not miss those two prayers.
now: Someone mocks your faith in the comments, or at the family dinner. You want to fire back. {idea}Patience, then prayer{/idea}, is the answer the Prophet ﷺ was given. It ends with being pleased.
old: When people mock me, I have to win the argument.
new: I can be patient, turn to prayer, and let Allah please me with what He gives.
try: Guard Fajr and Asr today especially, and notice how they frame your day.

title: Do not stare longingly at what others enjoy.
subtitle: Their splendor is a test
then: Umar once entered on the Prophet ﷺ in a small room with almost nothing in it, and {trap}wept, thinking of Kisra and Caesar in luxury{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}those people have had their good hastened for them in this world{/idea}. Mujahid said the groups meant here are the wealthy.
now: Scrolling past a friend's new kitchen, someone's luxury holiday, the influencer's car. Your own flat suddenly feels small. {reward}What your Lord gives is better and lasts longer.{/reward} Their shine is a test for them, and staring is a test for you.
old: If they have more than me, they are better off.
new: Their splendor is short and a test. My Lord's provision is better and lasting.
try: Mute or unfollow one account today that mostly makes you envious.

title: Call your family to prayer, and keep at it yourself.
subtitle: We provide for you, not you for Us
then: Ibn Kathir notes Umar would {idea}wake his family for night prayer{/idea}, reciting this verse. Allah says He does not ask provision from you, {reward}We provide for you{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ reported Allah saying: devote yourself to My worship and {reward}I will fill your chest with richness{/reward}.
now: You skip Dhuhr because the shift is busy and you need the hours. You do not wake the kids for Fajr because they are tired. {idea}Prayer is not what makes you poor.{/idea} The One you pray to is the Provider.
old: Taking time to pray, and getting my family to pray, costs me.
new: Allah does not need my provision; He gives it. Prayer opens the door.
try: Gently invite one family member to pray one prayer with you today.

title: Why no sign? The Quran itself is the sign.
subtitle: Demanding proof while holding it
then: They asked why Muhammad ﷺ did not bring a sign. Ibn Kathir says the Quran is that proof: revealed to {idea}an unlettered man who did not study with the People of the Book{/idea}, yet it tells the past and agrees with earlier scriptures. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}what I was given is revelation{/reward}.
now: You keep waiting for a sign before you take faith seriously: a dream, a miracle, a clear answer. {idea}The sign is already on your phone, on the shelf, in the app you opened today.{/idea}
old: I need a dramatic sign before I take this seriously.
new: The greatest sign is already in my hands. I just need to read it.
try: Read the last verses of this surah again slowly, as if they were the sign you asked for.

title: No one can say: if only someone had told us.
subtitle: The messenger removes every excuse
then: Ibn Kathir explains: had Allah destroyed them before sending the Prophet ﷺ, {trap}they would have said: if only You had sent us a messenger, we would have followed{/trap}. So the Messenger and the Book came, and {idea}the excuse was removed{/idea}.
now: You tell yourself, "Nobody ever taught me properly, my parents were not religious." Maybe true. But you are reading this now. {idea}It has reached you.{/idea} What you do next is yours.
old: I was never taught, so I cannot be expected to know.
new: The message has reached me now. From here, the choice is mine.
try: Learn one new thing about your faith today from a trustworthy source.

title: Everyone is waiting; you will see who walked straight.
subtitle: The surah ends with a calm challenge

row.title: it becomes clear
sub: who was on the straight path

then: Allah told the Prophet ﷺ to say to those who denied him: {idea}each of us is waiting, so wait{/idea}. You will come to know who is on {reward}the straight road{/reward} and who is guided. With this, the surah that began "not to distress you" ends without rush or anger.
now: Your relatives roll their eyes at your new habits. Your friends think you will drop them by next month. {idea}You do not have to win today.{/idea} Keep walking straight and let time show.
old: I have to prove I am right to everyone, now.
new: I can calmly keep to the straight path and let the truth reveal itself.
try: Leave one argument unfinished today, and just keep doing what is right.
